**Visual observations from test image:**
- Close-up of soybean leaf/petiole junction
- Petiole shows pronounced dark brown to near-black discoloration along its length
- Hairy stem texture with deep browning
- Leaf blade remains largely green with minor small spots
- The discoloration is most concentrated on the petiole/stem

**Key diagnostic feature:** The dark brown/black lesions running along a hairy petiole is characteristic of Anthracnose (*Colletotrichum truncatum*), which causes dark, irregular lesions on petioles and stems. The Anthracnose reference collage confirms this — bottom-left panel shows a hairy petiole with identical dark discoloration pattern matching the test image.

This matches the Anthracnose reference which displays the same pattern of dark lesions on hairy petioles/stems — a hallmark symptom of Colletotrichum truncatum infection. The leaf blade remains green, consistent with early-stage petiole-focused Anthracnose."}
